title: engine-loop lesson — a reusable rule (the harness state)
description: A lesson is a decision that has been generalised past its own occasion: it must be usable WITHOUT the episode in hand. It is the unit that gets injected back into the agent's harness (one file per lesson under harness_engine/memories/engine/), so the test for a good lesson is whether it changes behaviour on a DIFFERENT problem. `because` keeps it anchored to the observation that cost something; a rule with no cost attached is a platitude.

lesson_id.description: eng-<class abbreviation>-<4 digits>. Abbreviations: mh measurement-hygiene, lf log-forensics, diag diagnosis, gate gate-integrity, src source-reading, bound honest-bounds, perf performance, smoke smoke.

rule.description: Imperative and self-contained: a reader who has never seen the episode must be able to act on it. 'Be careful with numbers' is not a rule; 'Quote a delta only as the paired per-rep median of an interleaved A/B with >=3 rounds' is.

because.description: The specific observation that cost time or produced a wrong number, with the numbers. Anchors the rule so it can be re-litigated if the evidence changes.

counterexample_observed.description: episode_id or artifact where the rule was violated. A lesson that has never been violated in practice is usually not worth injecting.

applies_to.description: repo-relative paths (scripts, docs) the rule governs. This is what makes the lesson injectable at the right moment instead of as generic advice.
